new_statements.quote: Every word of two or more syllables (after you remove certain never-stressed word endings) is stressed on one of its last three syllables. Given the written word, you can tell which of the last three syllables is stressed by applying this Rule of Stress: If any syllable has a stressmark, that syllable is the one that is stressed. Otherwise, the word is stressed on the vocalic before the last consonant in the word (ignoring consonants in the word endings -as, -en, -ent, -er(s), -eux, -ic, -ica(s), -ici, -ilor, -laiset, -mint, -p(h)äts, and -sqab, if the word ends with one of those); If there is no such vocalic, the word is stressed on its first vocalic.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexically marked by a diacritic when irregular; otherwise it falls on the last closed syllable of the word (the vowel before the last consonant), computed after stripping a closed list of never-stressed suffixes, and always within the last three syllables; a word with no closed syllable is stressed on its first vowel. Default stress can therefore be final (cunceßetz), penultimate (cunceßent) or antepenultimate (cunceßadamint), as the ATLO page spells out.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; in hyphenated words each element carries its own stress (parta-t-o stressed on par and o).
new_statements.exceptions: Any stressmarked vowel overrides the rule; the never-stressed endings -as, -en, -ent, -er(s), -eux, -ic, -ica(s), -ici, -ilor, -laiset, -mint, -p(h)äts, -sqab are ignored (only the one the word actually ends with); words with no vocalic before a consonant (mici, ricas) take initial stress; optional unmarked final stress on 3sg future verbs (lirarha; serà obligatorily final); acest and vidarh optionally initial-stressed. The ATLO talossan.com page adds a slightly different ending list (-esch(en), -eu(x), -lor, -ttä) and umlaut vowels ä ö ü counting as stress-attracting, and cites embù and azul as optionally initial.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule for reading the standard orthography (Modern Orthography, post-2007) of a constructed language; the rule is stated over written words, and 'consonant' includes unstressmarked i/u before a vowel. Hyphenated compounds are stressed on each part separately (6.2). No phrase-level statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Talossan is an artificial language (Glottolog family 'Artificial Language', glottocode talo1253, ISO tzl). The quoted rule is the Kingdom of Talossa's standard 'Modern Orthography' adopted by the CÚG decree of 12 December 2007; pre-2007 'Classic' Talossan (Madison 1996 grammar) had no general stress rule and marked stress with assorted diacritics, and some writers (notably in the Republic of Talossa) retain that convention. Same glottocode; no separate code for the orthographic varieties. The catalog owner may want to exclude conlangs regardless.

sources.locator: Section 6.3 'The Stress Rule', PDF page 10 of 13 (document has no printed page numbers); text file lines 462-489
sources.note: Section 6 'Stress', 6.3 'The Stress Rule' (PDF p. 10): a stressmarked syllable is stressed; otherwise stress falls on the vocalic before the last consonant of the word, ignoring a closed list of never-stressed endings; if no such vocalic, the first vocalic; always within the last three syllables. Notes: i/u before a vowel count as consonants; optional unmarked final stress on 3sg future verbs; acest, vidarh optionally initial-stressed.

States that the Arestada sür Speliçaziun of 12 December 2007 'instituted a rule for stress that allowed many extraneous stressmarks to be omitted' and standardized stressmarks (acute/grave on a e i o u); lists later Arestadas 2010/XXXI, 2011/XXXII, 2014/XXXV (Arest10/11/) not fetched sources.

sources.citation: Association of Talossan Language Organisations (ATLO). 2012-2016. 'Stress', El Glheþ Talossan website (talossan.com), Phonology > Stress (WordPress page, copyright 2012 ATLO); Wayback captures 2015-05-31 and 2016-11-05
sources.note: 'THE STRESS RULE: If any syllable of a word contains a stress-marked vowel, then that syllable is stressed. Otherwise... Stress falls on the syllable containing the final vowel that is either marked with an umlaut (ä, ö, or ü) or followed by a consonant, after ignoring word-terminal -s and the word endings -en(s), -ent(s), -er(s), -esch(en), -eu(x), -ica(s), -ic(i), -(esch)laiset(s), -lor, -mint(s), -p(h)äts, and -sqab(s)'; post-vocalic i/u and e after a count as consonants; fallback first syllable (mici, troica, ricas); default stress can be final (cunceßetz), penult (cunceßent) or antepenul…

sources.citation: Comità per l'Útzil del Glheþ website (cuglang.com), 'About the CÚG' page (Wayback capture 2012)
sources.note: Historical note only: Talossan orthography 'had been criticised for a bewildering system of spoken stress and a myriad of diacritical marks', culminating in the 2007 Arestada 'instituting a stress rule'.

sources.citation: Kingdom of Talossa official website (kingdomoftalossa.net). 2011 (page last modified 14 Dec 2011). 'Emfasiçaziun Talossan / Talossan Stress' (New Spelling, post-Arestada 2007)
sources.note: Same rule restated: suffixes -mint, -laiset(s), -p(h)äts, -sqab and final -s, -lor, -x after eu, -en after consonant are ignored; 'Default stress falls on the final strong vowel', weak vowels being those in the endings -V(a), -(V)eu, -i(c)(V), -(i/u)ent, -er; words with only weak vowels (mici, ricas, diceux, vea) stressed on the first vowel; optional unmarked final stress on 3sg future verbs; acest, vidarh, embù optionally initial.

sources.note: Only that 4th-declension nouns take accent marks to show stress pattern: -ic never stressed, -íc always stressed, -ìc stressed in singular but shifting one syllable left in the plural (revîndic/revîndici, amíc/amíci, püblìc/püblìci); refers to a pronunciation section on p. 17 of the Treisoûr (dictionary).

sources.note: No general stress rule (pre-2007 'Classic' orthography, where stress was marked by a variety of diacritics). Introductory phonetics/orthography section (pp. 12-14 of the PDF) says only that final -â 'in fact is never stressed'; noun chapter (2.26) gives stress shifts in -ic/-ici plurals (penult in 2-syllable words, antepenult in longer); infinitive -arh stressed 'in the vast majority of verbs'.
